inputs.original_text: In a notable declaration, President John Mahama articulated that the foundational policies of the nation are intricately linked to its legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement. He emphasized his dedication to upholding the rule of law amidst the increasingly complex landscape of global discussions surrounding human rights. “I took an oath to uphold [...]
inputs.modified_text: Listen, let’s talk about what's really happening when those in power start talking about foundational policies and legal frameworks. President John Mahama wants us to believe that the system's rules are just naturally tied to our cultural ethos and collective agreement, but we know who writes these laws and whose interests they actually protect. When inequality is baked into the very institutions of society, simply talking about upholding the rule of law just means locking in the status quo that keeps marginalized and vulnerable communities down. He stands there and declares that he took an oath to uphold [...], but an oath to a structurally unjust system isn't enough when human rights are on the line globally. If we don't radically reform these institutions to center labor, justice, and true equity, this talk about legal frameworks is just smoke and mirrors designed to protect the powerful from accountability.
